title: Permission-aware AI: architecture and access
description: Conceptual six-layer architecture showing permission-aware context assembly. OKF provides structured knowledge, metadata and provenance: its primary conceptual home is layer 2, supporting context assembly at layer 4 and federation discovery at layer 5.

okf_role.summary: OKF informs source selection, context assembly and access decisions through structured knowledge and provenance; it does not enforce access or grant permissions.

supports.name: Agent orchestration
supports.role: Source selection, context assembly and provenance

okf_role.enforcement_distinction: Layer 3 represents security, identity and access enforcement, separate from OKF. Authorisation checks still operate across layers 2–4 and at each material transition.

alt_text: Six stacked architecture bands, numbered 6 to 1. A bracket spans layers 2–4. Dashed lines connect a separate OKF knowledge panel to layers 2, 4 and 5; layer 3 is labelled access enforcement, not OKF. The adjacent seven-step flow separates discovery, authorisation, context assembly, disclosure and actions.
authority_boundary: Independent exploratory research and conceptual placement, not government policy, implementation guidance, endorsement or evidence of implemented controls.
